items.followUp: What is meant by derived quantities and derived units?

rubric.why: Identifies base quantities as independent or fundamental physical quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that base quantities are independent/fundamental physical quantities.

rubric.why: Explains that base units are the units used to measure base quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that base units are standard units used to measure base quantities.

modelAnswer: Base quantities are independent physical quantities that are not defined in terms of other physical quantities.
Base units are the standard units used to measure base quantities.

rubric.why: States that a vector has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a vector has magnitude and direction.

rubric.why: States that a scalar has magnitude only and no direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a scalar has magnitude only, without direction.

modelAnswer: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.
A scalar quantity has magnitude only and no direction.

items.followUp: Explain how friction helps a vehicle stop when its brakes are applied.

rubric.why: Explains braking as using friction to reduce speed or stop motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that braking uses friction to slow down or stop a moving vehicle.

rubric.why: Identifies skidding as sliding rather than rolling normally.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that skidding occurs when the wheels or tyres slide along the road instead of rolling normally.

modelAnswer: Braking is the use of friction to slow down or stop a moving vehicle.
Skidding occurs when the wheels or tyres slide along the road instead of rolling normally.

items.followUp: Name two methods used to increase friction.

rubric.why: Gives one valid method of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming one valid method, such as lubrication, polishing surfaces, or using ball bearings.

rubric.why: Gives a second valid method of reducing friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a different valid method of reducing friction.

modelAnswer: Friction can be reduced by applying lubricants between surfaces.
Friction can also be reduced by using ball bearings.

items.followUp: What is meant by stable equilibrium?

rubric.why: Describes the body being given a small displacement from its equilibrium position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to a slight displacement from the equilibrium position.

rubric.why: Explains that the body moves farther from its original position, rather than returning.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that after displacement the body moves farther away or does not return to its original position.

modelAnswer: A body is in unstable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it moves farther away from its original position.
In this case, the centre of gravity of the body falls when it is displaced.

items.followUp: What is the difference between concurrent and non-concurrent forces?

rubric.why: Identifies like parallel forces as acting in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that like parallel forces act in the same direction.

rubric.why: Identifies unlike parallel forces as acting in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: What is meant by sound energy?

rubric.why: Identifies light as a form of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light is a form of energy.

rubric.why: States that light enables vision or produces the sensation of sight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that light enables us to see objects or produces the sensation of sight.

modelAnswer: Light is a form of energy.
It enables us to see objects and produces the sensation of sight.

items.followUp: A machine does 600 J of work in 20 s. Calculate its power and state the SI unit.

rubric.why: Defines power as the rate of doing work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining power as work done per unit time.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit of power as the watt, equivalent to one joule per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving watt (W) as the SI unit.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
The S.I. unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is equal to one joule per second (1 W = 1 J/s).
